---
title: "Which columns are numeric, categorical, or missing?"
---

## The question

Which columns are numeric, categorical, or missing?

## What to check and do

1. Load your table. 2. Call ru_columns() to inspect names, data types and missing counts. 3. Select a method only after checking the relevant fields.

## Worked example: airquality

This example uses a public dataset distributed with R. It does not make claims about observations outside that dataset.

```{r}
#| eval: false
d <- ru_data("airquality")
details <- ru_apply("inspect_columns", data=d)
stopifnot(any(details$column=="Ozone"), any(details$missing>0))
```

The air-quality table contains numeric weather variables and missing measurements. A column's existence does not mean every row contains a usable value.

## Apply the method to another question

Replace the data frame and column names with those in your own file:

```r
ru_columns(your_data)
```

If the variable is stored as character text, correct the import or encoding; do not blindly coerce it to numeric.


## Inspect conditions

Use `ru_plan("inspect_columns")` for available-versus-missing input routes. A calculation can run even when its assumptions do not justify an inference.
